Appendix A
One loop masters

In this appendix we give the expressions for the masters required for the Reverse Unitarity calculation detailed in sect.
V.3
as well as the region integrals required for the discontinuity calculation of sect.
V.2
.

A.1
Cut masters

As mentioned in sect.
V.3
, the Reverse Unitarity calculation takes the virtual bubble
B(p^{2})
, the cut bubble
\not{B}(p^{2})
and the doubly-cut triangle
\not{T}(p_{1}^{2},p_{2}^{2},p_{3}^{2})
as inputs. The virtual bubble is obtained straight-forwardly by Feynman parametrisation

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}B(p^{2})=\int\mathrm{d}^{d}k\frac{1}{k^{2}(p-k)^{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{\frac{d}{2}}\Gamma\left(\frac{d-2}{2}\right)^{2}\Gamma\left(\frac{4-d}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(d-2\right)}(-p^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}

\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{2-\epsilon}\Gamma\left(1-\epsilon\right)^{2}\Gamma\left(\epsilon\right)}{\Gamma\left(2-2\epsilon\right)}(-p^{2})^{-\epsilon}

(221)

where we set
d=4-2\epsilon
. The cut bubble and the doubly cut triangle are obtained by direct integration in momentum space:

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}\not{B}(p^{2})=\int\mathrm{d}^{d}k\tilde{\delta}^{+}(k)\tilde{\delta}^{+}(p-k)

\displaystyle=-\frac{2^{4-d}(p^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}\pi^{\frac{d+3}{2}}}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d-1}{2}\right)}\Theta(p^{0})\Theta(p^{2})

\displaystyle=-\frac{2^{2\epsilon}(p^{2})^{-\epsilon}\pi^{\frac{7}{2}-\epsilon}}{\Gamma\left(\frac{3}{2}-\epsilon\right)}\Theta(p^{0})\Theta(p^{2}),

(222)

For the cut triangle we find

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}\not{T}(p_{1}^{2},p_{2}^{2},p_{3}^{2})

\displaystyle=\int\mathrm{d}^{d}k\,\tilde{\delta}^{-}(k)\tilde{\delta}^{+}(k+p_{1})\tilde{\delta}^{+}(k-p_{3})

\displaystyle=-4\mathrm{i}\frac{(-p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}p_{3}^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}}{\lambda(p_{1}^{2},p_{2}^{2},p_{3}^{2})^{\frac{d-3}{2}}}\frac{\pi^{\frac{d}{2}+2}}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}-1\right)}\Theta(-p_{1}^{0})\Theta(p_{1}^{2})\Theta(p_{3}^{0})\Theta(p_{3}^{2})

\displaystyle=-4\mathrm{i}\frac{(-p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}p_{3}^{2})^{-\epsilon}}{\lambda(p_{1}^{2},p_{2}^{2},p_{3}^{2})^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}}\frac{\pi^{4-\epsilon}}{\Gamma\left(1-\epsilon\right)}\Theta(-p_{1}^{0})\Theta(p_{1}^{2})\Theta(p_{3}^{0})\Theta(p_{3}^{2}),

(223)

where
\lambda(x,y,z)=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}-2xy-2xz-2yz
is the Källen function.

A.2
Calculation of
T_{h}

The hard function
T_{h}
required in the region expansion of sect.
V.2
is simply the two-mass triangle, which IBP-reduces to bubbles:

T_{h}(p,q)=\frac{(d-3)[B(q)-B(p+q)]}{(d-4)p\cdot(p+q)}.

(224)

Using the result for the bubble of eq. (
221
):

(2\pi)^{d}T_{h}(p,q)=\mathrm{i}\pi^{d/2}\frac{\Gamma(1-\epsilon)^{2}\Gamma(\epsilon)}{\Gamma(2-2\epsilon)}\frac{(d-3)[(-q^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}-(-(p+q)^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}]}{(d-4)p\cdot(p+q)}.

(225)

A.3
Calculation of
T_{c}

The collinear function
T_{c}
required in the region expansion of sect.
V.2
is computed in light-cone coordinates. It reads:

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}(-p_{1}^{2})^{-\epsilon}T_{c}(p_{1},p_{2})=

\displaystyle\int\mathrm{d}^{d}k\frac{1}{k^{2}(k-p_{1})^{2}(2k^{+}(n_{+}\cdot p_{2})+p_{2}^{2})}\,.

(226)

Where we have used light-cone variables,
k=k^{+}\hat{n}_{+}+k^{-}\hat{n}_{-}+k_{\perp}
,
\hat{n}_{\pm}\cdot k_{\perp}=0
,
\hat{n}_{\pm}^{2}=0
and
\hat{n}_{+}\cdot\hat{n}_{-}=2
. The integral
T_{c}
corresponds to the leading collinear region in the
p_{1}^{2}
expansion of the three-mass triangle. Changing to light-cone coordinates and performing contour integration in
k^{-}
, we have, assuming
p^{+}_{1}>0

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}(-p_{1}^{2})^{-\epsilon}T_{c}=

\displaystyle\mathrm{i}\pi\int_{0}^{1}\mathrm{d}t\int\mathrm{d}^{d-2}\vec{k}_{\perp}\frac{1}{(p_{1}^{2}t(t-1)+|\vec{k}_{\perp}|^{2})(2t(p_{1}\cdot p_{2})+p_{2}^{2})}.

(227)

where we have introduced
t=k^{+}/p_{1}^{+}
. The integral in
|\vec{k}_{\perp}|
is trivial to perform in terms of a beta function. After integration in
|\vec{k}_{\perp}|
and in the solid angle associated with the
\mathrm{d}^{d-2}\vec{k}_{\perp}
integration, we obtain:

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}(-p_{1}^{2})^{-\epsilon}

\displaystyle T_{c}(p_{1},p_{2})=-\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{d/2+1}(p_{1}^{2})^{d/2-2}\csc((d-4)\pi/2)}{\Gamma(d/2-1)}\int_{0}^{1}\mathrm{d}t\frac{\left[t(t-1)\right]^{d/2-2}}{2t(p_{1}\cdot p_{2})+p_{2}^{2}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{d/2+1}\csc(-\epsilon\pi)\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}{(-p_{2}^{2})\Gamma(2-2\epsilon)}(-p_{1}^{2})^{-\epsilon}{}_{2}F_{1}\left[1,1-\epsilon,2-2\epsilon,\frac{2p_{1}\cdot p_{2}}{-p_{2}^{2}}\right].

(228)

In the last step we have set
d=4-2\epsilon
. One may expose the non-analiticities in the argument of the hypergeometric function by usual means. For example, when
p_{1}=p
,
p_{2}=q
, the hypergeometric function is evaluated at
1/x
, which for
x\in(0,1)
introduces non-analiticities:

\displaystyle(2\pi)^{d}(-p^{2})^{-\epsilon}T_{c}(p,q)=

\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{d/2+1}\csc(-\epsilon\pi)\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}{(-q^{2})\Gamma(2-2\epsilon)}(-p^{2})^{-\epsilon}{}_{2}F_{1}\left[1,1-\epsilon,2-2\epsilon,\frac{1}{x}\right]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle-\frac{\mathrm{i}\pi^{d/2+2}\csc(-\epsilon\pi)^{2}}{(-q^{2})\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}(-p^{2})^{-\epsilon}x\Bigg[(x-1)^{-\epsilon}x^{-\epsilon}

\displaystyle+\frac{\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}{\Gamma(1-2\epsilon)\Gamma(1+\epsilon)}{}_{2}F_{1}\left[1,2\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1-x\right]\Bigg].

(229)

Now the result is expressed in terms of a hypergeometric function that is analytic for
x\in(0,1)
.

Appendix B
Double discontinuity of two-loop three-point master integrals at leading virtuality

One direct way of computing the iterated discontinuities of the two-loop three-point master integrals is by expressing them in terms of the different unitarity cuts of their underlying diagrams. To this end, let us define the following four cut integrals

\displaystyle F_{1}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})

\displaystyle=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}^{d}k\mathrm{d}^{d}l}{\pi^{d}}\delta^{-}(k)\delta^{-}(l)\frac{\delta^{+}(l-p_{3})\delta^{+}(k+p_{1})}{[(k+l+p_{1})^{2}]^{\alpha_{1}}[(k+l-p_{3})^{2}]^{\alpha_{2}}},

(230)

\displaystyle F_{2}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})

\displaystyle=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}^{d}k\mathrm{d}^{d}l}{\pi^{d}}\delta^{-}(k)\delta^{-}(l)\frac{\delta^{+}(l-p_{3})\delta^{+}(k+l+p_{1})}{[(k+p_{1})^{2}]^{\alpha_{1}}[(k+l-p_{3})^{2}]^{\alpha_{2}}},

(231)

\displaystyle F_{3}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})

\displaystyle=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}^{d}k\mathrm{d}^{d}l}{\pi^{d}}\delta^{-}(k)\delta^{-}(l)\frac{\delta^{+}(k+l-p_{3})\delta^{+}(k+l+p_{1})}{[(k+p_{1})^{2}]^{\alpha_{1}}[(l-p_{3})^{2}]^{\alpha_{2}}},

(232)

\displaystyle F_{4}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})

\displaystyle=\int\frac{\mathrm{d}^{d}k\mathrm{d}^{d}l}{\pi^{d}}\delta^{-}(k)\delta^{-}(l)\frac{\delta^{+}(k+l-p_{3})\delta^{+}(k+p_{1})}{[(k+l+p_{1})^{2}]^{\alpha_{1}}[(l-p_{3})^{2}]^{\alpha_{2}}}.

(233)

where
\delta^{\pm}(q)=\delta(q^{2})\Theta(\pm q^{0})
. The double discontinuity of any of the three-point master integrals can be expressed as a linear combination of these four functions. In particular:

\displaystyle\text{disc}_{p_{1}^{2}}

}}=F_{4}(0,0).

(240)

One important check that this construction implies is pole cancellation. Discontinuities are finite as long as all the invariants are not zero, and thus

\displaystyle F_{1}(1,1)+2(F_{2}(1,1)+F_{3}(1,1)+F_{4}(1,1))=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{0}),

(241)

\displaystyle F_{2}(0,1)+F_{3}(0,1)=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{0}),

(242)

\displaystyle F_{1}(1,0)+F_{2}(1,0)+F_{4}(0,1)=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{0}),

(243)

\displaystyle F_{2}(0,0),F_{4}(0,0)=\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{0}).

(244)

We performed the integration at leading
p_{1}^{2}
virtuality of the
F_{i}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})
functions:

\displaystyle F_{1}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})

\displaystyle=\frac{(p_{3}^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}(p_{1}^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}}{\pi^{2}(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})^{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}}\left[\frac{\beta\left(\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{1},\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{2}\right)}{\Gamma(d/2-1)}\right]^{2},

(245)

\displaystyle F_{2}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})=\frac{(p_{3}^{2})^{d-3-\alpha_{1}}(p_{1}^{2})^{d-3-\alpha_{1}}}{\pi(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})^{d-2+\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{1}}}\left[\frac{\beta\left(\frac{d-2}{2},\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{1}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}-1\right)}\right]^{2}\csc\left(\alpha_{1}\pi-\frac{d\pi}{2}\right)\times

\displaystyle\times\Bigg(-\frac{\Gamma\left(-1+\frac{d}{2}\right)\phantom{}_{2}F_{1}\left[1-\alpha_{1},2+\alpha_{2}-\frac{d}{2},-\alpha_{1}+\frac{d}{2},\frac{p_{3}^{2}}{-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3}}\right]}{\Gamma(\alpha_{1})\Gamma\left(-\alpha_{1}+\frac{d}{2}\right)}+\left[\frac{-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3}}{p_{3}^{2}}\right]^{d/2-\alpha_{1}-1}\times

\displaystyle\times\frac{\Gamma\left(-1-\alpha_{2}+\frac{d}{2}\right)\phantom{}_{2}F_{1}\left[3+\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}-d,2-\frac{d}{2},2+\alpha_{1}-\frac{d}{2},\frac{p_{3}^{2}}{-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3}}\right]}{\Gamma(-2-\alpha_{1}-\alpha_{2}+d)\Gamma\left(2+\alpha_{1}-\frac{d}{2}\right)}\Bigg),

(246)

\displaystyle F_{3}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})=-\frac{(-p_{2}^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}(p_{3}^{2})^{d-3-\alpha_{2}}(p_{1}^{2})^{d-3-\alpha_{1}}}{\pi(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})^{\frac{3}{2}d-4}}\left[\frac{\beta\left(\frac{d-2}{2},\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{1}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}-1\right)}\right]^{2}e^{i\left(1+\alpha_{2}-\frac{d}{2}\right)\pi}\times

\displaystyle\times\left(-i+\cot\left(\alpha_{2}\pi-\frac{d\pi}{2}\right)\right)\frac{\Gamma\left[-1+\frac{d}{2}\right]\phantom{}_{2}F_{1}\left[\alpha_{1},\frac{d}{2}-1-\alpha_{2},-2-\alpha_{2}+d,\frac{p_{3}^{2}}{(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})}\right]}{\Gamma\left[2+\alpha_{2}-\frac{d}{2}\right]\Gamma[-2-\alpha_{2}+d]},

(247)

\displaystyle F_{4}(\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2})=\frac{(p_{3}^{2})^{d-3-\alpha_{2}}(p_{1}^{2})^{\frac{d-4}{2}}}{\pi(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})^{\frac{d}{2}-1+\alpha_{1}}}\left[\frac{\beta\left(\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{1},\frac{d-2}{2}-\alpha_{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}-1\right)}\right]^{2}\left(-i+\cot\left(\alpha_{2}\pi-\frac{d\pi}{2}\right)\right)\times

\displaystyle\times e^{i\left(1+\alpha_{2}-\frac{d}{2}\right)\pi}\frac{\Gamma\left[-1+\frac{d}{2}\right]\phantom{}_{2}F_{1}\left[2+\alpha_{1}-\frac{d}{2},\frac{d}{2}-1-\alpha_{2},-2-\alpha_{2}+d,\frac{p_{3}^{2}}{(-2p_{1}\cdot p_{3})}\right]}{\Gamma\left[2+\alpha_{2}-\frac{d}{2}\right]\Gamma[-2-\alpha_{2}+d]}.

(248)

All four results truncate higher orders in
p_{1}^{2}
.

Appendix C
Embedding tables and description of supplementary material

In this appendix we tabulate all the embeddings that have been computed in order to obtain the next-to-leading order structure functions for deep inelastic scattering. Each row corresponds to an embedding of a vacuum diagram. The first cell of each row provides the winding numbers with respect to a reference cycle basis. In other words, it allows to reconstruct the tuple
(G,\mathbf{w})
belonging to
\mathrm{Emb}_{\mathrm{dis}}
. The chosen reference cycle bases for the two vacuum graphs are:

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\text{DT}}

\displaystyle=\{d_{1},d_{2},d_{3},d_{4}\}=\left\{\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_DT_b1.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_DT_b2.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_DT_b3.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_DT_b4.pdf}}\right\},

\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\text{SE}}

\displaystyle=\{c_{1},c_{2},c_{3},c_{4}\}=\left\{\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_SE_b1.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_SE_b2.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_SE_b3.pdf}},\raisebox{-25.60747pt}{\includegraphics[]{Submission/appendix_drawings/gen_SE_b4.pdf}}\right\}.

The second and third cell of each row provide one selected forward-scattering diagram compatible with the embedding (namely one choice of rooted cut), with
a_{1}
or
a_{2}
being the initial-state electron, respectively. In other words, the second and third cell may be mapped to the two possible thruples
\Gamma=(G,\mathbf{w},a_{1})
and
\overline{\Gamma}=(G,\mathbf{w},a_{2})
obtained by supplementing the winding information with a choice of initial-state electron. The forward-scattering diagrams are routed according to the simplest clustering criterion, imposing that the sum of partons momenta in the initial state is
p
. By applying Feynman rules to each forward-scattering diagram (including the cutting rules for the initial-state particles), and promoting all cut propagators to ordinary Feynman propagators, we obtain the integrand of the embedding,
\tilde{I}_{\Gamma}
and
\tilde{I}_{\overline{\Gamma}}
. The loop integration variable which in the main text is labelled as
k
is, in the drawings, labelled by either
k_{2}
or
k_{3}
, depending on the embedding.

We also provide the embedding integrand information in two separate
.m
files as ancillary material. Each file contains a list of embedding relating to one of the two vacuum graphs. Say they have been assigned the names

dataSE=Import["path_to_file/dataSE.m"];

dataDT=Import["path_to_file/dataDT.m"];

Each element of the list is an association list, corresponding to a defined embedding
(G,\mathbf{w})
. For example, calling

dataSE[[1]][["embedding"]]

gives

{1,0,-1,1}

as output. Thus
dataSE[[1]]
corresponds to the embedding of the self-energy vacuum diagram with winding number
\mathbf{w}=(1,0,-1,1)^{T}
. The choices of initial-state electron
\Gamma
and
\bar{\Gamma}
can be obtained by instead calling

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]]

and

dataSE[[1]][["a2"]]

which yield two separate association tables (the entry is not present when there is no rooted cut for that embedding cutting the selected electron and satisfying
r_{e}\leq 1
for all
e
). In particular,

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]][["Denominator"]]/.k[x_]:>k

gives the propagator structure of
I_{\Gamma}
as a product of
prop[m,p]
=\frac{1}{p^{2}-m^{2}}
,

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]][["Numerator"]][["F2"]]/.k[x_]:>k

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]][["Numerator"]][["FL"]]/.k[x_]:>k

give the numerator of
I_{\Gamma}
projected on the structure functions
F_{2}
and
F_{L}
(
G
and
eq
being the strong and electric coupling constants,
Nc
the number of colours,
TF
the normalisation of the
T^{a}
matrices and
dim
=d=4-2\epsilon
the dimensional regulator) and

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]][["Numerator"]][["zero"]]/.k[x_]:>k

gives the numerator of
I_{\Gamma}
contracted with
q^{\mu}q^{\nu}
. The substitution rule
/.k[x_]:>k
makes sure that in both propagators and numerators, the integration variable is labelled by
k
, instead of
k[2]
or
k[3]
depending on the embedding. Finally

dataSE[[1]][["a1"]][["Cut content"]]

gives the cut content
\mathfrak{q}_{\Gamma}
of the embedding.
